text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Bomb kills 12 in a car market in Boufarik, south of Algiers.
- The state budget allows 11.9 billion dinars ($212 million) for social safety net to alleviate economic reform impact on the poor in 1997.
- workers'Union Generale des Travailleurs Algeriens (UGTA) holds talks with state-owned company managers over salaies.
- Bomb kills 13 in Boufarik's car market.
- The government to set an independent election watchdog body.
- Bomb kills 14 in a car market in Boufarik.
- Security forces kill four "terrorists" at the High Casbah in Algiers.

- Secular opposition Socialist Forces Front (FFS) leader Debaili Mustpaha says "the government was pushing opposition party leaders to dissolve themsleves their movements." He referred to what opposition alleges that the authorities were blocking their activities.
- Algiers chides Tripoli over an idea of Libyan mediation between Islamists and the authorities.
